title: OSHA 1910.27 Scaffold and Rope Descent System Checklist
subtitle: Use at the start of each workshift a rope descent system will be used, and when checking a general industry scaffold.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item fails, do not start or continue the descent or scaffold work until it is corrected; take damaged or defective equipment out of service and replace it.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Scaffolds and anchorage records
items: Any scaffold in use has been checked against subpart L (Scaffolds) of 29 CFR part 1926.
Written statement from the building owner that each anchorage is identified, tested, certified and maintained to support at least 5,000 pounds (2,268 kg) in any direction for each employee attached.
The owner's information is based on an annual inspection by a qualified person.
Each anchorage has been certified by a qualified person as necessary and within the last 10 years.
The employer had the written anchorage information before any employee used an anchorage.
The anchorage information is retained and available for the whole duration of the job.

sections.title: Conditions before descent
items: Work is not above 300 feet (91 m) above grade, or the employer has demonstrated other means are not feasible or pose a greater hazard.
Where the descent is greater than 130 feet (39.6 m), stabilization is in place at the specific work location.
No storms, gusty or excessive wind or other hazardous weather at the time of use.
Every employee using the system has been trained in accordance with § 1910.30.
The system was inspected at the start of this workshift.
Use matches the manufacturer's instructions, warnings and design limitations, or is directed by a qualified person.

sections.title: Equipment, rigging and ropes
items: No damaged or defective component in use; any found has been removed from service and replaced.
Every component other than the seat board is rated to sustain a minimum load of 5,000 pounds (22.2 kN).
Seat board is capable of supporting a live load of 300 pounds (136 kg).
Anchorages and tiebacks rigged properly; tiebacks fitted wherever counterweights, cornice hooks or similar non-permanent anchorages are used.
Padding or other protection on ropes at every point they can touch building edges, the anchorage, obstructions or other surfaces.
Ropes kept away from open flames, hot work, corrosive chemicals and other destructive conditions.

sections.title: Fall arrest, rescue and dropped objects
items: Each employee is connected to a separate, independent personal fall arrest system meeting subpart I of part 1910.
Arrangements are in place to rescue each employee promptly after a fall.
Tools, squeegees, buckets and similar equipment are secured by tool lanyards or a similar method.

references: 29 CFR 1910.27: Scaffolds and rope descent systems (Part 1910 Subpart D: Walking-Working Surfaces)
